info.cls_ename: Department of Foreign Languages and Literature

description.describe_ch: 這門課的主要重點是藉由課堂上不同的活動，來增進學生的英文單字量、文法分析與閱讀理解。過程當中，也會帶領同學們學習不同的閱讀技巧，來強化同學們的閱讀能力。除了單字、文法以及閱讀能力的強化外，亦將透過特定主題，來選取不同背景之文章來進行授課，以期厚實學生的文化底蘊。
description.describe_eh: This course aims to improve students’ vocabulary, grammar, and reading abilities through various kinds of in-class activities. In order to achieve this goal, teachers will also introduce different reading strategies to enhance students’ reading comprehension. In terms of students’ cultural cultivation, teachers will choose articles revealing different cultural values.

gradeRuleDescribe.tpa_score_new:
Class participation [presence and active participation] – 40% of your grade
 
Mid-term Paper  (30%) - due week 9
 
Final Report and project (30%) - due week 15
 
‣ Meetings will be scheduled between Week 4 - 8 - Students will be invited to present the project for their midterm paper or presentation as a group or individually.
‣ Starting from Week 5, students are required to follow the assigned reading schedule and complete both a story outline and a reflection report during class.
 
This class requires academic exercise, which includes:  
‣Your library visit due week 6 
‣ Members of group and presentation topics should be decided de reported to me by Week 10
‣ Your draft of ppt or materials for group presentations due week 13
‣ Week 16 and 17, are designed for group presentations
 
‣ For mid-term paper, students are expected to hand in a keyword research paper. Approx. 500 words.
Note that regular in-class quizzes will be conducted throughout the course. Completing a minimum number of these quizzes is a requirement to be eligible to submit the midterm report. Students who do not meet this requirement will not be permitted to hand in their midterm.
Students will also present your mid-term paper and your topic in class.
 
‣ For final report, you will be graded on how well you have integrated feedback as well as the 
elements of narrative we studied in class into you paper and your work in progress.
This part of the grade will also reflect  your ability to write and express yourself in English: grammar, lexicon, syntax, style, fluidity,  voice and creativity. 
 
＊The course plan may be adjusted as needed throughout the semester＊
gradeRuleDescribe.course_pol:
- The group meetings scheduled to take place during Weeks 4 to 5, as well as the report outlines that require preliminary review, must be submitted in hard copy.
- All questions regarding the course should be raised during class sessions. Students are expected to pay attention to announcements and explanations provided in class, including course rules. Please refrain from asking the professor to repeat information that has already been clearly explained or presented during lectures.
- Regular in-class quizzes will be conducted throughout the course. Completing a minimum number of these quizzes is a requirement to be eligible to submit the midterm report. Students who do not meet this requirement will not be permitted to hand in their midterm.
- Starting from Week 5, students are required to follow the assigned weekly reading schedule and complete both a story outline and a reflection report during class.
- Recording, filming, and photography are prohibited in class without prior consent

gradeRuleDescribe.course_pol_en:
綜合說明
In this English class, students are expected to follow academic guidelines.
Your final grade will be based on both individual work and group work, and both components are equally important. While you may be stronger in one area, keep in mind that your evaluation includes both.
It is essential to arrive on time, especially during group presentations, as punctuality affects the whole group and your presentation is assessed as a team.
You are also expected to listen actively to your classmates’ presentations and provide thoughtful feedback when requested. 
Plagiarism of any kind is strictly prohibited. If you choose to use AI tools, you must explain how you used them in your process—otherwise, do not use them at all. These rules are in place to promote respect, responsibility, and academic honesty in our learning community.
